evals.prompt: I'm running thin-edge on a fleet of gateways that also run nginx as a reverse proxy. I want to be able to push nginx config updates from the cloud. Write me a tedge config plugin (shell is fine) that manages the main nginx config at /etc/nginx/nginx.conf. nginx can validate a config with `nginx -t` and you reload it with `systemctl reload nginx`. Call the config type `nginx`.
evals.expected_output: A POSIX shell config plugin implementing list/get/prepare/set/verify/rollback for type `nginx`. list prints `nginx`; get prints the effective config (cat /etc/nginx/nginx.conf or `nginx -T`); prepare validates with `nginx -t` on the candidate and backs up the current config to --work-dir; set installs the new file and reloads via systemctl; verify checks nginx is active; rollback restores the backup and reloads. Correct exit codes and stderr usage. Plus install + local test instructions.
assertions: Implements all six config-plugin subcommands — list, get, prepare, set, verify, and rollback — dispatched from the plugin's command handler.
`list` prints the config type name `nginx` (one per line) and nothing else.
The prepare, set, verify, and rollback subcommands accept and use the `--work-dir <dir>` argument.
`prepare` only validates the candidate and backs up the current config into the work-dir — it does NOT apply the new config or restart any service.
`set` applies the new config and reloads nginx via systemctl, exiting non-zero (so the agent triggers rollback) if that fails.
`rollback` restores the backup that prepare saved in the work-dir and reloads/restarts the service.
On failure, subcommands write a message to stderr and exit non-zero; stdout is reserved for get/list output.
Provides install instructions (copy to /usr/share/tedge/config-plugins, make executable) and local test commands exercising the subcommands.
`prepare` validates the candidate nginx config using `nginx -t` before accepting it.
The service reload uses `systemctl reload nginx`.

evals.prompt: We deploy an internal app on our edge devices configured via an env file at /etc/acme-agent/agent.env (KEY=VALUE lines). The app runs as the systemd unit acme-agent.service. There's no real config validator for it, but the file must be parseable as key=value pairs. I'd like thin-edge to manage this `agent.env` config type so ops can update it remotely and have the service restart. Can you write the config plugin?
evals.expected_output: A config plugin (default shell) for type `agent.env`. get prints /etc/acme-agent/agent.env. prepare validates the candidate file parses as KEY=VALUE lines (since no native validator exists, a lightweight syntactic check is appropriate) and backs up the current env file to --work-dir. set moves the new file into place and `systemctl restart acme-agent`. verify checks the unit is active. rollback restores the backup and restarts. Handles the no-validator case sensibly rather than faking one. Includes install/test steps.
assertions: Implements all six config-plugin subcommands — list, get, prepare, set, verify, and rollback — dispatched from the plugin's command handler.
`list` prints the config type name `agent.env` (one per line) and nothing else.
The prepare, set, verify, and rollback subcommands accept and use the `--work-dir <dir>` argument.
`prepare` only validates the candidate and backs up the current config into the work-dir — it does NOT apply the new config or restart any service.
`set` applies the new config and restarts the acme-agent service, exiting non-zero (so the agent triggers rollback) if that fails.
`rollback` restores the backup that prepare saved in the work-dir and reloads/restarts the service.
On failure, subcommands write a message to stderr and exit non-zero; stdout is reserved for get/list output.
Provides install instructions (copy to /usr/share/tedge/config-plugins, make executable) and local test commands exercising the subcommands.
Because acme-agent has no native validator, prepare validates the candidate by checking it parses as KEY=VALUE lines, rather than inventing/calling a non-existent validator.
`set` restarts the `acme-agent` systemd service after applying the new env file.

evals.prompt: I want to extend thin-edge config management to handle my Mosquitto broker. The interesting part is the effective config is split across /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf plus a bunch of fragment files in /etc/mosquitto/conf.d/*.conf, and when someone reads the config from the cloud I want them to see the combined effective configuration, not just the main file. Updates should replace the main mosquitto.conf and restart the mosquitto service. Write the plugin for a config type called `mosquitto`.
evals.expected_output: A config plugin for type `mosquitto` where get outputs the merged effective config (main file + conf.d/*.conf fragments concatenated, ideally with markers showing source), not just the main file. prepare backs up the main config (and accounts for restore), set replaces /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf and restarts mosquitto, verify confirms the broker is running, rollback restores. Demonstrates the multi-fragment aggregation requirement of get. Includes install/test steps.
assertions: Implements all six config-plugin subcommands — list, get, prepare, set, verify, and rollback — dispatched from the plugin's command handler.
`list` prints the config type name `mosquitto` (one per line) and nothing else.
The prepare, set, verify, and rollback subcommands accept and use the `--work-dir <dir>` argument.
`prepare` only validates the candidate and backs up the current config into the work-dir — it does NOT apply the new config or restart any service.
`set` applies the new config and restarts the mosquitto service, exiting non-zero (so the agent triggers rollback) if that fails.
`rollback` restores the backup that prepare saved in the work-dir and reloads/restarts the service.
On failure, subcommands write a message to stderr and exit non-zero; stdout is reserved for get/list output.
Provides install instructions (copy to /usr/share/tedge/config-plugins, make executable) and local test commands exercising the subcommands.
`get` outputs the combined effective configuration — the main /etc/mosquitto/mosquitto.conf plus the /etc/mosquitto/conf.d/*.conf fragments merged together — not just the main file.
`set` replaces the main mosquitto.conf and restarts the mosquitto service.
